$comment: Gate thresholds for CI. Same quality metrics as gate.json; NO resource metrics.
Selected with `npm run eval:run -- --gate-config eval/config/gate.ci.json`; see .github/workflows/eval.yml.
WHY LATENCY AND COST ARE NOT GATED HERE, and this is not a convenience.
gate.ts already says a resource comparison is only meaningful between runs with
matched cache state, and CI cannot supply that. Three things stack up on a runner:
1. THE CACHE IS ALWAYS COLD ON A NEW GOLDEN SET. The actions/cache key is keyed on
questions.dev.jsonl, so the first run after any golden-set change starts at zero
hits — while eval/baselines/ci-smoke.jsonl was snapshotted from a warm local run.
2. THE FREE-TIER APIS RATE-LIMIT. A cold run means real embed calls, which means 429s
and 20-40s backoff waits. That time lands in embedMs and therefore in totalMs.p95.
3. SHARED RUNNERS VARY. Even warm, a hosted runner is not a stable clock.
MEASURED, not hypothetical. On the first green CI run of this workflow both smoke jobs
failed on totalMs.p95 alone — 20637ms -> 462217ms (+2140%) on retrieval, and 20637ms ->
306630ms (+1386%) on generation — while EVERY quality metric was unchanged to the tenth
of a point: recall@10 43.4% -> 43.4%, correctness 52.0% -> 52.0%, faithfulness and
refusalAccuracy 100% -> 100%. The gate was measuring the rate limiter, not the pipeline.
A gate that fails for reasons unrelated to the diff is a gate people learn to ignore —
the same reasoning that split this workflow into two jobs in the first place. Latency
regressions are real and worth catching; catch them locally with gate.json, where you
control cache state, or with `npm run eval:sweep`. Do not re-add them here without
first making both sides of the comparison cache-matched.
